interpretation: Operational completion improved by 1 percentage point (38 to 39); no prior completion was lost.
Two formerly unavailable claims now select CMS1500 but stop at unchanged safety checks. This is not end-to-end recovery.
One previously unsafe claim now completes; its selection route changed from REGISTRATION_CONFIDENCE to ANCHOR_MATCH on the same page and template.
All completed claims still require field review. Review demand increased by one completed claim; the completed-claim review rate stayed 100%.

Latency is observed single-pass wall time, including fresh process startup, dataset verification, I/O and reached stages. It is not an isolated normalization microbenchmark or a statistical performance guarantee.
limits: Existing uncommitted workspace changes were retained identically to the baseline; measured source hashes identify the implementation.
Baseline provider/environment version hashes were not recorded; this comparison used the same local Python environment without installing or changing providers.
FinalClaim completion concerns the selected page; it does not establish extraction accuracy or complete multipage-claim understanding.
No benchmark, tuning, threshold change, runtime code modification or claim retry performed.

metric_definitions.operational_completion: Application SUCCESS and COMPLETED FinalClaim for the matching document.
metric_definitions.registration_success: Application registration stage SUCCESS, excluding selector probe successes.
metric_definitions.selection_unavailable: Application registration UNAVAILABLE with no selected template.
metric_definitions.safety_failure: Final selected registration attempt terminates with SafetyFailure; selector probes excluded.
metric_definitions.review_required: FinalClaim.review_required is true; unreached decisions are unknown, not approvals.
metric_definitions.latency: Parent process total_time_ms / 1000; percentiles use linear interpolation at (n-1)*p.
